title: t3 (null-weight-shuffled): the checkpoint does not perform the labelled behaviour; no circuit claimed
label: no behaviour found (null result)
behavior: BOS + 5 tokens from 6 symbols (ba, ka, ne, se, va, ve); the model is said to output one symbol (D, E or M) at the last position, with dataset answers equal to the model's own outputs.
summary: On local-full (full precision) the loaded checkpoint reproduces the dataset's answers on 4% of 200 inputs, on two independent seeds (E0002, E0003). That is below 3-way chance. The logit difference between labelled answer and foil has mean near zero relative to a standard deviation of about 4100, and the top-1 prediction is often an input symbol (va, ve) rather than an output symbol. There is therefore no behaviour to explain: no function, no circuit and no predict() are claimed, and verification was deliberately not run. The investigation stopped after 3 of 25 experiments.

claims.text: The checkpoint does not reproduce the dataset answers: clean accuracy 0.04 on 200 inputs (seed 1), logit diff mean -107, std 4096. The pre-registered prediction of >=0.99 accuracy was refuted.
The failure replicates on an independent sample: clean accuracy 0.04 on 200 inputs (seed 2), logit diff mean -281, std 4097; pre-registered prediction of <=0.2 confirmed.
No attention head or MLP layer is claimed as part of a circuit, because there is no above-chance behaviour for a circuit to implement.

limitations: Only the baseline was measured; no component-level experiments were run, since without a behaviour their effects would be uninterpretable.

The 64 dataset labels seen in E0001 mostly fit 'E if count(se) > count(ka), M if count(ka) > count(se), D if equal' (62/64 by hand). This describes the labels only, was not tested against the model, and is not a claim about this checkpoint.
Accuracy of 4% is below 1/3 chance over D/E/M, consistent with the model often predicting tokens outside the output set; the distribution of its predictions was not characterised further.
open_questions: Why do the dataset answers not match this checkpoint's outputs: is the checkpoint a weight-shuffled null of the model that generated the labels?
Does the checkpoint compute any structured function of its input at all, or are its outputs effectively arbitrary?
overall_status: unverified (no verification run) · no behaviour found (null result)

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: The model deterministically outputs one of D/E/M at the last position; since dataset answers are its own outputs, baseline accuracy is ~1 with a clear positive logit margin.

prediction.statement: clean accuracy against the model's own answers is at least 0.99
